newsitem.title: USA: Reno told by FBI in May about China allegations.
newsitem.headline: Reno told by FBI in May about China allegations.

text.p: Attorney General Janet Reno said on Thursday the FBI told her in May about possible Chinese efforts to funnel money to congressional candidates in the 1996 elections, and she thought the information had been properly passed on to the White House.

Reno also said she had ordered an internal review arising from the "misunderstanding" between the FBI and the White House National Security Council that resulted in the information not being given to President Bill Clinton.
After she was briefed by the FBI in May, Reno said it had been decided that she would call then-White House National Security Adviser Tony Lake.

"I was not able to reach Lake, and told them (the FBI) to make sure the briefing went forward and assumed that the briefing would take place -- everybody would be briefed," she said at her weekly Justice Department news conference.
She repeated her explanation that at the June briefing the FBI agents placed no restrictions on disclosing the information to other officials, but did say it involved a sensitive matter.

Clinton said on Monday he had learned of the allegation only recently because the White House National Security Advisers thought FBI agents did not want them to pass the information to Clinton or other senior officials.
